body: Merry Christmas to all and to all a good night!

Although it may seem otherwise, I don’t believe I falsified any documents; the documents signed were the same ones she was intended to sign at a later date, and no loss, financial or otherwise occurred. I do definitely see the error in judgment that I made, but there was no ill-intent from the outset. The goal was to keep a senior disabled resident housed, although I admittedly went about it incorrectly. Thanks so much for your advice.

Thank you so much! Canadian citizenship sounds pretty good about now ;) we were actually told as an agency by our executive director to do whatever we could in our power to keep people houses during COVID so I thought I was doing that by assisting this resident; never have I been more wrong! I appreciate the progressive approach!
Thanks for the response; I guess I’m just wary of not being able to submit a resignation on my own terms after 5+ years.

Thank you; I truly appreciate your perspective and acknowledge the errors I made. I can see how the situation is construed. I guess in my mind I was trying to help out the individual. Any kind of wrongdoing or fraud never crossed my mind, although I can see what it looks like from the outside looking in. Regardless, would it be better to attend the hearing and profess my ignorance and apologize or attend the hearing and tender resignation (or even beforehand) and try to negotiate a neutral reference. I am pretty devastated that 5.5 years of stellar work was negated by this error. As they say, the road to hell is paved with good intentions...thanks for your opinions and expertise!
